title: Support/resistance zones — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's full review of PR #147 (backend-support-resistance), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: Efficiency: `detect_support_resistance_zones` (app/signals/support_resistance.py) runs the full O(n) break/false-breakout scan (`_scan_breaks_and_false_breakouts`) and the `_dollar_volume` window computation for every candidate cluster before sorting by `strength_score` and truncating to `max_zones` (15) -- even though the sort key only depends on the cheap `length_category`/`height_category`. A ~20-year daily history produces ~104 candidate clusters while only 15 are ever returned, so most of that scan work is thrown away on every GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis call for a long-history ticker. Consider scoring/sorting candidates first and only running the expensive scan on the top `max_zones` survivors.

docs/architecture/Backend.md §2's module-layout tree wasn't updated to list the new app/signals/support_resistance.py module under signals/, unlike prior tasks that added a new module to this same list (e.g. indicators/autoenvelope.py, indicators/_validation.py). Add it.

_cluster_touches's sequential merge-by-running-mean can chain: each new point is compared against the cluster's current (shifting) mean rather than its original anchor, so an unbroken sequence of touches each within 1% of the running mean can end up spanning noticeably more than 1% end-to-end. Not a bug (upper/lower are still the cluster's actual price extremes), but this known limitation of naive sequential 1-D clustering isn't acknowledged in the task's decisions entry (which only compares against k-means/density alternatives on complexity/auditability grounds). Consider documenting this explicitly or tightening to an anchor-based tolerance check.

decisions.decision: Efficiency fix: deferred the expensive per-candidate work (`_scan_breaks_and_false_breakouts`'s O(n) forward scan and `_dollar_volume`'s window aggregation) until after candidates are ranked and truncated to `max_zones`, by splitting the old single `_build_zone` pass into a cheap `_score_candidate` (height_pct/length_days/length_category/height_category/strength_score only) used for sorting, and a `_build_zone` that now only runs on the surviving top-`max_zones` candidates. Verified via backend/tests/unit/signals/test_support_resistance.py (all 15 existing tests, unmodified assertions, pass against the refactored implementation, including the pre-existing `test_max_zones_caps_the_returned_list` cap test) and full-suite pytest --cov=app (741 passed, app/signals/support_resistance.py 100% line+branch).
decisions.rationale: The task's own checklist item explicitly flags the risk that the expensive computation might feed the ranking criteria, in which case naive reordering wouldn't be safe -- read `_strength_score`'s definition and the sort key (`zones.sort(key=lambda z: (z.strength_score, z.touch_count, z.last_touch_date), ...)`) closely first and confirmed neither `broken`/`break_date`/`false_breakout` (from the break scan) nor `dollar_volume` appears in that key or in `_strength_score`'s own composite (length_category + height_category only, per the original task's decisions entry -- dollar_volume is deliberately excluded from strength_score there too, for its own separate reason: no book-given absolute thresholds to classify it against). `touch_count`/`last_touch_date`, the other two sort-key fields, already exist on the candidate dict straight out of `_cluster_touches`, before any per-zone scan ever runs. So which candidates survive the cap, and their final order, is provably identical to the old 'score everything then sort/truncate' pipeline; only candidates that get truncated away now skip the expensive scan entirely -- a pure performance win with zero behavior change. Rejected alternative: memoizing/caching `_scan_breaks_and_false_breakouts` results across repeated calls instead of reordering -- rejected as solving a different problem (repeated-call cost) than the one actually reported (wasted work within a single call, on candidates that never make the top 15 at all).

decisions.decision: Chain-drift in `_cluster_touches`: kept the existing sequential merge-by-running-mean behavior as-is (not switched to anchor-based tolerance), and instead (a) documented the limitation explicitly in `_cluster_touches`'s own docstring, and (b) added a regression test (`TestClusterTouchesChainDrift::test_running_mean_merge_can_drift_a_clusters_span_beyond_tolerance_pct`) that hand-demonstrates a 3-point cluster where each merge step is individually within the 1% tolerance of the running mean at that point, yet the cluster's final end-to-end span (100.0 to 101.45, i.e. 1.45%) exceeds the nominal 1% tolerance.
decisions.rationale: This is judged an acceptable, non-blocking documented limitation rather than something requiring a fix, for several reasons: (1) it is not a correctness bug against this module's own contract -- `upper`/`lower` are always the cluster's genuine touch-price extremes, never fabricated or extrapolated, so a zone's boundaries are still real, auditable price levels a trader could see on a chart; 'tolerance_pct' was always documented as governing each individual merge decision, not a hard cap on the resulting cluster's total width. (2) The book (Elder ch. 18) gives no numeric tolerance at all, let alone a stated guarantee about a zone's total span versus a per-touch tolerance -- there's no methodology requirement being violated. (3) Switching to anchor-based comparison (compare each new point to the cluster's FIRST point, not its running mean) is a real behavior change, not just a bugfix: it would produce more, smaller clusters in cases where prices drift gradually across a wide congestion band, potentially splitting what a trader would still recognize as one wide zone into several disconnected minor ones -- an equally defensible interpretation, but not obviously superior, and it would change the already-hand-verified fixture assertions in the original task's tests (e.g. `TestCleanMultiTouchZone`'s 108.8/109.0/109.3 zone) in ways that would need re-justifying from scratch. Given the finding itself was filed as non-blocking by pr-reviewer, and 'is an acceptable, documented limitation' is one of the two options this task's checklist explicitly offers, documenting + regression-testing the current behavior (so it can never silently change without a test noticing) was chosen over a speculative behavior change with no clear methodology mandate behind it. Rejected alternative: switch to anchor-based tolerance (compare every point in a cluster to its first point rather than the running mean) -- rejected per the above; noted here as the natural change to make later IF a real-world false-negative/false-positive zone-boundary case is ever actually observed, rather than pre-emptively now on a purely theoretical concern.

comments.summary: Efficiency refactor (checklist item 1) is provably equivalent to the old pipeline: the sort key (strength_score, touch_count, last_touch_date) never depends on the deferred _scan_breaks_and_false_breakouts/_dollar_volume work, confirmed independently both by re-reading the code and via a standalone synthetic simulation of 40 multi-strength-score candidates showing old-pipeline vs new-pipeline order/truncation are identical. However, the only in-repo test that exercises the max_zones cap (test_max_zones_caps_the_returned_list) truncates a list of a single qualifying candidate with max_zones=1 -- it never exercises reordering across multiple distinct-strength-score candidates, so it would not actually catch a ranking-order regression in this refactor. Non-blocking (independently verified correct by this review) but tracked as a follow-up so the equivalence claim gets real in-repo regression coverage rather than relying on reviewer-external reasoning.

Chain-drift finding (checklist item 3): reviewed the new docstring and TestClusterTouchesChainDrift regression test independently rather than deferring to the task-worker's decision. The 'keep as documented limitation' call is correct: docs/Analyse.md's row 9 description states the 1% tolerance governs each merge decision, not a hard cap on a cluster's total span, and gives no numeric guarantee about end-to-end zone width -- so there is no methodology violation. upper/lower remain genuine touch-price extremes (never fabricated), and the regression test's arithmetic is correct (100.9 is +0.90% of 100.0; 101.45 is +0.995% of the running mean 100.45, both within the 1% tolerance, producing a 1.45% total span as asserted). Accepted as-is.

review.notes: Verified independently rather than trusting the PR's own claims: backend full suite 741 passed, app/signals/support_resistance.py 100% line+branch coverage, overall backend coverage 99.92% (gate 90%) -- re-ran myself, not just read the PR description. ruff check app/ and mypy both clean. No frontend/openapi.json changes in this PR (pure internal backend refactor + docstring/test additions), and openapi.json is correctly untouched since no route/schema signature changed. docs/architecture/Backend.md already lists support_resistance.py (satisfied by a prior commit on this branch, confirmed present). Both checklist items phrased as judgment calls have corresponding `decisions` entries with rationale -- no undocumented decision gap. code-review skill (medium effort) found zero correctness/reuse/simplification/efficiency issues. Browser walkthrough performed (this PR affects an existing endpoint -- GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis -- with a live frontend consumer, so step 9 applies): started backend (fixture data provider) + frontend dev servers, drove a real headless Chromium through the AAPL stock-analysis page plus an unknown-ticker edge case; support/resistance zones render on the price chart in sensible, correctly-sorted order, zero console errors, zero failed network requests. Also ran the persisted e2e suite (make e2e): all 16 specs across dashboard/navigation/portfolio/stock-analysis/watchlist passed. One non-blocking finding (see comments) filed as a new follow-up task backend-support-resistance-followups-followups since none existed yet for this task id.
